pathway.title: BIOMARIN PHARMACEUTICAL INC — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Leverage is the dominant credit issue and its true size cannot be measured from the supplied documents. Net debt moved from a net cash position at the 2025 year end to USD 3,437.68 million, which is 9.07x trailing reported EBITDA, or 9.26x with the USD 3,507.68 million pro forma figure for the October 2026 licence payment. The trailing EBITDA holds Amicus from 2026-04-27 only, so the ratio is too high on a full-year basis, but no pro forma earnings are printed to say by how much, and the company reports covenant compliance against a maximum total net leverage ratio of 3.50x whose definition is not supplied. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_bmrn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 50; calculation C1

Interest is the transmission channel. Coupon interest in the third quarter, the first full quarter with the new debt, was USD 52.68 million, or USD 210.73 million annualised, against USD 69.72 million of cash interest paid in the trailing twelve months. Trailing reported EBITDA covers the annualised coupon 1.80x and, before the acquired research charge, 3.16x; the third quarter alone covered cash interest 0.78x and, before the charge, 5.39x. These are analyst figures that mix periods, shown to size the burden, not covenant ratios. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_bmrn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C3

Cash generation is the main support. Operating cash flow was USD 576.97 million and free cash flow after plant and equipment purchases USD 498.94 million in the nine months to 2026-09-30, down 20.78% and 25.09% from a year earlier; the company attributes the lower operating cash flow mainly to lower net income and the timing of payments to vendors, partly offset by lower inventory purchases. Free cash flow excludes the USD 277.88 million paid for acquired research assets and the USD 5,067.63 million paid for Amicus, so it measures operating capacity, not total cash after deals. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_bmrn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bmrn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47; calculation C5

Growth is mostly acquired and the largest product is slowing. Revenue rose 18.49% in the nine months, but without the USD 336.42 million Amicus products contributed it rose 4.15%; VOXZOGO, 28.78% of 2025 revenues, grew 9.78% in the nine months after 26.10% in 2025. The three largest products were 68.43% of 2025 revenues, so diversification is average, not strong. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_bmrn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-K_2025-12-31_bmrn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 209; calculation C6; calculation C7

Liquidity and the 2027 maturity look manageable. Cash of USD 736.01 million alone covers the USD 660.00 million due in 2027 1.12x and cash plus the undrawn revolver covers it 2.02x; the USD 600.00 million convertible notes due in May 2027 had a fair value of 97.65% of principal, which suggests cash repayment rather than conversion. The revolver depends on covenant compliance that cannot be tested, so cash is the firmer cushion, and pro forma cash after the October 2026 licence payment is not established. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C2

Financial policy is restrained on distributions and active in acquisitions. The company has paid no dividend and made no buyback, pre-funded the acquisition notes into escrow and cut the bridge to zero, but it bought three businesses and licensed a programme in barely more than a year and ranks secured lenders ahead of the convertible holders. Business & governance rates owner behaviour medium risk, and this analysis agrees. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_bmrn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 22–25

cells.text: Develops, makes and sells medicines for rare genetically defined diseases; one operating segment run on consolidated net income

Eight commercial therapies at 2025 year end (VOXZOGO, VIMIZIM, NAGLAZYME, PALYNZIQ, ALDURAZYME, BRINEURA, KUVAN, ROCTAVIAN); GALAFOLD and POMBILITI + OPFOLDA added on 2026-04-27; ROCTAVIAN no longer marketed
Net product sales to specialty pharmacies, distributors, wholesalers, hospitals and governments; ALDURAZYME sold only to Sanofi, which pays 39.5% to 50% of its net sales
Three customers were 37% of 2025 net product revenues and 36% in nine months 2026; one customer was 20% of receivables at 2026-09-30
United States 34.88% and Europe 27.60% of 2025 net product revenues; more than 75% of VOXZOGO revenue is outside the United States
Active ingredients made at Novato, California and Shanbally, Cork; some raw materials come from a sole or single source
2025 research and development 28.62% of revenues and selling, general and administrative expense 35.79%; 3,221 employees at 2025-12-31
Amicus consolidated from 2026-04-27; Alesta from 2026-08-31 (asset acquisition)

runs.text: Strength: cash generation. Operating cash flow of USD 576.97 million and free cash flow of USD 498.94 million in nine months, with purchases of plant and equipment at only 3.20% of 2025 revenues, give the company internal funds for interest and scheduled amortisation, which supports deleveraging and the 2027 repayment. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_bmrn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 183–184; calculation C5

Strength: liquidity and a pre-funded structure. Cash of USD 736.01 million, an undrawn revolver of USD 600.00 million and escrowed acquisition notes mean no funding gap before the May 2027 maturity, which lowers refinancing pressure; pro forma cash after the October 2026 licence payment is not established. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C2

Strength: a diversified rare-disease franchise with exclusivity into the 2030s. Nine commercial therapies, VOXZOGO patents to 2035 and 2036 and orphan exclusivity to 2030, and acquired Fabry and Pompe products, reduce the risk that one product loss stops debt service. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bmrn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 23–25; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Weakness: leverage. Net debt of USD 3,437.68 million at 9.07x trailing reported EBITDA, or USD 3,507.68 million and 9.26x pro forma for the October 2026 licence payment, with annualised coupon interest of USD 210.73 million, leaves a thin cushion against an earnings shortfall until Amicus earnings are fully counted. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C3

Weakness: concentration and order timing. VOXZOGO is 28.78% of revenues, three customers are 37% of net product revenues and large international orders move between quarters, so a delayed order can swing cash and covenant tests in a single quarter. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-11-02_earningsrelease-2nov26ex991.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C6

Weakness: ranking and unseen covenants. The secured term loans rank ahead of the senior unsecured notes and the subordinated convertible notes as to collateral, and the covenants that limit further deals and distributions are not supplied, so subordinated holders carry risk they cannot measure. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_bmrn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 22–25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bmrn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 50

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The Amicus acquisition was agreed on 2025-12-19 as an all-cash merger at USD 14.50 per share, and completed on 2026-04-27. Total consideration was USD 5,323.561 million, including USD 432.920 million to repay Amicus' own debt, accounted for as a business combination with preliminary allocations of USD 4,750.000 million to intangible assets and USD 469.786 million to goodwill. The price was funded by new non-convertible debt and about $1.7bn of cash. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_bmrn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14–16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bmrn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bmrn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 123; 10-Q_2026-03-31_bmrn-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 24

The new debt is USD 850.0 million of 5.5% senior unsecured notes due 2034, a USD 800.0 million senior secured term loan A due 2031-04-27, a USD 2.0 billion senior secured term loan B due 2033-04-27 and a USD 600.0 million senior secured revolver due 2031-04-27 that is undrawn. The credit agreement of 2026-04-27 names Citibank, N.A. as administrative and collateral agent and lists issuing banks, which points to a letter-of-credit facility whose size is not printed. A supplemental indenture of the same date lists guarantors, so the 2034 notes may carry subsidiary guarantees that the filings do not describe. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_bmrn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 22–25; 10-Q_2026-03-31_bmrn-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 111; 10-K_2025-12-31_bmrn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 226

Smaller transactions are Inozyme (2025-07-01, asset acquisition, USD 285.0 million net of cash acquired), Alesta (2026-08-31, asset acquisition, USD 303.4 million, with up to USD 215 million of milestones), a Fabry licence in October 2026 (USD 70.0 million upfront, up to USD 405.0 million of milestones) and the Ascendis settlement. BioMarin also assumed a licence with Dimerix with milestones of up to USD 510.0 million. Pro forma nine-month revenue as if Amicus had been owned from 2025-01-01 is USD 3,009.554 million against USD 2,780.562 million reported; no pro forma earnings are printed. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bmrn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 225; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bmrn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bmrn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bmrn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: BIOMARIN PHARMACEUTICAL INC (bmrn), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the financial foundation: statements, debt, net debt, liquidity and calculated credit metrics from the supplied filings and earnings releases. The statements cover FY2024, FY2025, nine months 2025 and nine months 2026, with the balance sheet at three dates.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: BioMarin went from net cash at the 2025 year end to net debt of USD 3,437.68 million at 2026-09-30 after buying Amicus, and its reported earnings do not yet carry that debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt is 9.07x reported EBITDA of USD 378.82 million for the twelve months to 2026-09-30. That base holds Amicus for only about five months and absorbs a USD 287.69 million acquired research charge, so it overstates leverage, but no pro forma EBITDA or covenant calculation is supplied to show by how much. Liquidity is USD 1,336.01 million of cash and an undrawn revolver, and USD 660.00 million of principal falls due in 2027, mostly convertible notes in May.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: At the 2025 year end the only debt was the USD 600.00 million convertible notes due in 2027, carried at USD 597.18 million, against cash of USD 1,311.68 million, so net debt was negative USD 714.50 million, that is net cash. During 2026 the company raised USD 3,650.00 million (USD 850.00 million of senior unsecured notes and USD 2,800.00 million of senior secured term loans), repaid USD 15.00 million and paid USD 5,067.63 million of cash, net of cash acquired, for Amicus. Principal debt reached USD 4,235.00 million at 2026-09-30, carried at USD 4,173.69 million, and cash fell to USD 736.01 million. Reported total debt to EBITDA therefore moved from 1.22x at 2025 to 11.02x on the twelve months to 2026-09-30, and net leverage from net cash equal to 1.46x EBITDA to net debt of 9.07x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The trailing figure is not a clean measure of the new group. BioMarin states no EBITDA, so it is built as income from operations plus depreciation and amortization: USD 489.04 million for 2025 and USD 378.82 million for the twelve months to 2026-09-30, although revenue rose from USD 3,221.25 million to USD 3,655.13 million. The window absorbs integration and restructuring costs and acquired research charges while counting Amicus only from 2026-04-27: Amicus contributed revenue of USD 336.42 million and a net loss of USD 239.38 million, and the nine months carry restructuring charges of USD 113.59 million, acquisition-related costs of USD 32.80 million and inventory step-up amortization of USD 29.20 million. Printed pro forma figures give revenue and net loss as if Amicus had been owned from 2025-01-01 but no pro forma EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash interest cover was 67.50x in 2025 and 5.43x on the twelve months to 2026-09-30, but the trailing ratio understates the new burden because it holds only about five months of interest on the new debt. In the third quarter alone, the first full quarter with Amicus, cash interest paid was USD 62.33 million against reported EBITDA of USD 48.38 million, a cover of 0.78x; before the acquired research charge of USD 287.69 million, which is mostly the Alesta asset purchase, the same quarter covered interest 5.39x. A single quarter is lumpy because the first semi-annual coupon on the 2034 notes fell due on 2026-08-15; interest expense in the quarter, which payment timing does not affect, was USD 55.63 million. USD 2,785.00 million of term loans float, and the company states that a rise of 100 bp in rates would add about USD 27.9 million a year to interest expense.

fields.value: Operating cash flow was USD 576.97 million in the nine months to 2026-09-30 against USD 728.35 million a year earlier, and free cash flow after purchases of property, plant and equipment was USD 498.94 million against USD 666.03 million, 123.81% of nine-month reported EBITDA. Cash conversion exceeds EBITDA because reported EBITDA is struck after stock-based compensation of USD 172.68 million and the acquired research expense of USD 282.26 million, neither of which reduces operating cash flow. The measure flatters debt service capacity, because it excludes USD 277.88 million paid for acquired research assets and USD 5,067.63 million for Amicus, both investing outflows.

fields.value: Liquidity at 2026-09-30 was USD 1,336.01 million: cash of USD 736.01 million plus the USD 600.00 million senior secured revolving facility, which is undrawn and runs to April 2031. The sources state the full capacity is available and name no letters of credit against it. Marketable securities, USD 741.17 million at the 2025 year end, were nil. No facility expires within twelve months. The balance sheet shows USD 658.72 million of debt as current, which is consistent with the 2027 convertible notes plus the next four quarters of term loan repayments, USD 60.00 million, less unamortized costs; the rest of the term debt falls due from 2031. Firm purchase commitments of USD 768.80 million, USD 291.10 million of them due in 2026, also draw on cash.

fields.value: The new debt is mostly secured. The term loans of USD 2,785.00 million carry first-priority liens on substantially all assets of the company and its subsidiary guarantors and rank ahead of the USD 850.00 million senior unsecured notes and the USD 600.00 million senior subordinated convertible notes. Secured principal is 7.35x trailing reported EBITDA and all principal debt is 11.18x. The term loans amortise by USD 60.00 million a year in total, and the guarantors are described only as certain subsidiaries.

fields.value: The company reports compliance at 2026-09-30 with a maximum total net leverage ratio of 3.50x, temporarily 4.00x for certain acquisitions, and a minimum interest coverage ratio of 3.00x, which apply to the term loan A and the revolver. The ratios, their definitions and the headroom are not printed, and the credit agreement is not supplied, so the 9.07x above cannot be compared with the covenant and no headroom is calculated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: BioMarin defines a non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA as income from operations excluding depreciation, amortization and stock-based compensation but prints no value for it. Applying that definition to the trailing period gives USD 598.42 million and net debt of 5.74x; also adding back the acquired research charge gives USD 886.10 million and 3.88x. These are analyst calculations for scale only, not company figures, and covenant EBITDA may differ.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: One event after the balance sheet date changes net debt: in October 2026 the company agreed to license an experimental Fabry disease treatment for an upfront payment of USD 70.00 million, to be expensed as acquired research in the fourth quarter, with up to USD 405.00 million of milestones. If the upfront payment is made in cash, pro forma net debt is USD 3,507.68 million, or 9.26x trailing reported EBITDA; the payment date is not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence that leverage is less severe than the trailing ratios show is the company's statement that it met its covenants at 2026-09-30, which allow net leverage of 3.50x to 4.00x, and its stated aim of gross leverage below 2.50x by mid-2027, supported by about USD 280.00 million of expected GAAP cost synergies fully realised in 2028. Free cash flow of USD 498.94 million in nine months, and revenue guidance of USD 3,800.00 million to USD 3,900.00 million for 2026, point the same way. Reported EBITDA is also depressed by USD 287.69 million of acquired research charges that reflect discretionary pipeline purchases rather than the earnings of the marketed products: before them, trailing net leverage is 5.16x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Against that, no covenant ratio, pro forma EBITDA or definition is available to confirm the headroom, the cash interest in the trailing window is only a part of the new run-rate, and further acquired research charges are already coming: the upfront licence payment of USD 70.00 million in the fourth quarter and up to USD 405.00 million of milestones. The view would improve with disclosure of covenant EBITDA and ratios, with a fourth quarter showing a full quarter of Amicus and a lower interest burden relative to EBITDA, or with a refinancing of the USD 600.00 million convertible notes due in May 2027. It would worsen if the third quarter cover of 5.39x before acquired research charges fell as interest costs rise, or if the 2027 notes had to be repaid from cash rather than refinanced.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: BIOMARIN PHARMACEUTICAL INC (bmrn), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the business, ownership, transaction, operating model, governance and sponsor-behaviour facts a creditor needs, taken from the seven supplied filings and earnings releases. No ranking, instrument view or recovery view is given.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: BioMarin is a publicly held rare-disease drug maker with no controlling owner or sponsor in the sources, so creditors face operating, acquisition and financing risk rather than owner extraction risk, and the Amicus purchase has made that risk larger.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The largest product, VOXZOGO, was 28.78% of 2025 revenues and three customers bought 37% of net product revenues. The company counts four transactions in 2026 that added development programs, and the largest was paid for mostly with new secured debt; the board, holder and covenant detail that would limit further deals sits in documents that are not supplied. Owner behaviour is therefore rated medium risk on incomplete evidence, not low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bmrn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_bmrn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 18; EX-99.1_2026-11-02_earningsrelease-2nov26ex991.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bmrn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 22–25; calculation C1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No controlling owner or sponsor appears in the sources, which removes dividend recapitalisation and fee leakage as documented risks but leaves control rights unestablished. The company states that it has never paid a cash dividend, made no issuer repurchases in the fourth quarter of 2025 and shows none in its statements of equity, and it had 28 holders of record. Holders above five percent, board independence and related-party dealings are in a proxy statement that is not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bmrn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 148; 10-K_2025-12-31_bmrn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 172; 10-K_2025-12-31_bmrn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 183; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash flow rests on one growth product and a few buyers. VOXZOGO produced USD 926.92 million, 28.78% of 2025 revenues, grew 26.10% in the year and earns more than 75% of its revenue outside the United States; three customers took 37% of net product revenues, and Sanofi is the only customer for ALDURAZYME (6.47% of revenues). VOXZOGO has United States orphan exclusivity that expires in 2028 for older children and 2030 for younger ones and a composition patent extended to 2035, but named clinical-stage competitors are developing rival treatments for achondroplasia.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bmrn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_bmrn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19; 10-K_2025-12-31_bmrn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 23–25; 10-K_2025-12-31_bmrn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 209; EX-99.1_2026-11-02_earningsrelease-2nov26ex991.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C1; calculation C3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Acquisition is now the main use of cash and it is mostly debt funded. The company bought Inozyme in July 2025 for USD 285.00 million net of cash acquired, closed Amicus in April 2026 for USD 5,323.56 million of total consideration, bought Alesta in August 2026 for USD 303.44 million and agreed a licence in October 2026 with an upfront payment of USD 70.00 million. New borrowings of USD 3,650.00 million and about $1.7bn of cash paid for Amicus, so about two thirds of the price was borrowed. The company counts four transactions in 2026 that added programmes, and its appetite for further deals is the main thing the supplied documents cannot bound.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bmrn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 225–226; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bmrn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14–19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bmrn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bmrn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47; EX-99.1_2026-11-02_earningsrelease-2nov26ex991.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The financing moved ranking against the existing creditors. The 2027 convertible notes are senior subordinated, unsecured and expressly effectively subordinated to secured debt, and the new secured term loans carry first-priority liens on substantially all assets of the company and its guarantors; the unsecured revolver that existed at the 2025 year end was terminated in April 2026 and replaced by a secured one. That was disclosed and expected in the notes' terms, so it is a ranking fact and not evidence of coercive treatment, but the convertible holders now sit behind a much larger secured claim.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Pre-funding was structured to protect noteholders. The senior unsecured notes were issued in February 2026 into escrow and had to be redeemed at par if the Amicus acquisition did not close by 2026-12-19, and the bridge commitment fell from $3.7bn to $2.8bn and then to zero as permanent debt replaced it. No dividend, buyback or related-party payment is documented in the supplied pages.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Acquired pipeline spending has already produced a write-off. The lead Inozyme asset cost an acquired research expense of USD 220.96 million in 2025 and its development was discontinued in August 2026, about 13 months after the purchase, and the 2025 decision to withdraw ROCTAVIAN carried about USD 240.00 million of restructuring charges. Both were charged to earnings in the year and left no asset behind, which shows that purchased programmes can fail quickly.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bmrn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; 10-K_2025-12-31_bmrn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 225; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bmrn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bmrn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 42–43; calculation C5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reporting is regular and audited, with gaps around the new business. The auditor, KPMG, has served since 2002 and gave an unqualified opinion on the 2025 statements and on internal control, with one critical audit matter on ALDURAZYME variable consideration; a clawback policy dates from October 2023. Controls at Amicus are still being integrated and the Amicus purchase accounting is preliminary, so reported results for the acquired business carry more estimation risk than the legacy business.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The operating model is high-margin but heavy on discretionary spending. In 2025 research and development was 28.62% of revenues, 21.76% before the acquired research expense, selling, general and administrative expense was 35.79% of revenues and capital spending was 3.20%. Much of that spending is discretionary, which gives management room to cut if earnings fall while interest is contractual, but large international and government orders arrive unevenly: a big VOXZOGO order moved from the third to the fourth quarter of 2026 and the company cut its 2026 revenue guidance to USD 3,800.00 million to USD 3,900.00 million from USD 3,875.00 million to USD 3,925.00 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The competing product now pays a royalty. The settlement agreed with Ascendis in late August 2026 licenses BioMarin's patents for Ascendis' Yuviwel in exchange for 20% of United States net sales and 18% in the European Union, Brazil and South Korea until May 2030. That reduces patent-litigation uncertainty and gives BioMarin income from a rival, but it confirms that a competing product is on the market.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for a lower risk rating is the record of financial policy. The company has never paid a dividend, made no buybacks in 2025, settled the 2024 convertible notes in cash at maturity, entered 2026 with net cash, kept the new revolver undrawn and states a target of gross leverage below 2.50x by mid-2027, with about USD 280.00 million of GAAP cost synergies expected by 2028. Annual reporting is audited and internal control was effective at the 2025 year end.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Against a lower rating, four facts weigh more. The acquisition replaced a single convertible note with secured term loans and new unsecured notes within five months; the credit agreement that limits further deals, distributions and extra debt is not supplied; management says it will keep expanding the pipeline through business development; and Amicus integration and controls are unfinished. The view would move to low risk on evidence of restrictive covenants and a second reporting period of falling leverage with no further large debt-funded deal, and to high risk on a debt-funded distribution, a large further debt-funded acquisition, or a change in the holder base that put control in one party's hands.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The Amicus acquisition was agreed on 2025-12-19 as an all-cash merger at USD 14.50 per share, and completed on 2026-04-27. Total consideration was USD 5,323.561 million, including USD 432.920 million to repay Amicus' own debt, accounted for as a business combination with preliminary allocations of USD 4,750.000 million to intangible assets and USD 469.786 million to goodwill. The price was funded by new non-convertible debt and about $1.7bn of cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The new debt is USD 850.0 million of 5.5% senior unsecured notes due 2034, a USD 800.0 million senior secured term loan A due 2031-04-27, a USD 2.0 billion senior secured term loan B due 2033-04-27 and a USD 600.0 million senior secured revolver due 2031-04-27 that is undrawn. The credit agreement of 2026-04-27 names Citibank, N.A. as administrative and collateral agent and lists issuing banks, which points to a letter-of-credit facility whose size is not printed. A supplemental indenture of the same date lists guarantors, so the 2034 notes may carry subsidiary guarantees that the filings do not describe.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Smaller transactions are Inozyme (2025-07-01, asset acquisition, USD 285.0 million net of cash acquired), Alesta (2026-08-31, asset acquisition, USD 303.4 million, with up to USD 215 million of milestones), a Fabry licence in October 2026 (USD 70.0 million upfront, up to USD 405.0 million of milestones) and the Ascendis settlement. BioMarin also assumed a licence with Dimerix with milestones of up to USD 510.0 million. Pro forma nine-month revenue as if Amicus had been owned from 2025-01-01 is USD 3,009.554 million against USD 2,780.562 million reported; no pro forma earnings are printed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Module status: Ready with Limitations. Source quality is High for filed reports and Medium for issuer releases; no external source is used.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor / Governance Risk Level: Medium. The risk level is driven by the debt-funded Amicus acquisition and the repeated acquired research spending, because they raise interest and refinancing burden while ranking secured lenders ahead of existing holders, which implies lower recovery for unsecured and subordinated holders and less cushion for the 2027 refinancing. Countervailing evidence is the absence of any dividend or buyback, a pre-funded and escrow-protected financing and audited reporting. Further analysis requires the credit agreement, the indentures and the 2026 proxy statement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: BIOMARIN PHARMACEUTICAL INC (bmrn), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the integrated fundamental credit view: business quality, cash-flow durability, liquidity, refinancing capacity, financial policy, downside path and monitoring triggers. It rests on the supplied filings and releases and on the accepted outputs of Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: BioMarin's rare-disease franchises still generate operating cash, but the Amicus financing moved the company from net cash to net debt, and creditors now depend on integration lifting earnings before the 2027 convertible maturity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_bmrn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; calculation C1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt is USD 3,437.68 million at 2026-09-30, or USD 3,507.68 million pro forma for the October 2026 licence payment, which is 9.07x trailing reported EBITDA of USD 378.82 million, or 9.26x pro forma; that EBITDA holds Amicus for only about five months and a USD 287.69 million acquired research charge. Liquidity of USD 1,336.01 million covers the USD 660.00 million of principal due in 2027, so the near-term risk is earnings delivery under a covenant package that is not supplied, not a funding gap.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is the dominant credit issue and its true size cannot be measured from the supplied documents. Net debt moved from a net cash position at the 2025 year end to USD 3,437.68 million, which is 9.07x trailing reported EBITDA, or 9.26x with the USD 3,507.68 million pro forma figure for the October 2026 licence payment. The trailing EBITDA holds Amicus from 2026-04-27 only, so the ratio is too high on a full-year basis, but no pro forma earnings are printed to say by how much, and the company reports covenant compliance against a maximum total net leverage ratio of 3.50x whose definition is not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_bmrn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 50; calculation C1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Interest is the transmission channel. Coupon interest in the third quarter, the first full quarter with the new debt, was USD 52.68 million, or USD 210.73 million annualised, against USD 69.72 million of cash interest paid in the trailing twelve months. Trailing reported EBITDA covers the annualised coupon 1.80x and, before the acquired research charge, 3.16x; the third quarter alone covered cash interest 0.78x and, before the charge, 5.39x. These are analyst figures that mix periods, shown to size the burden, not covenant ratios.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_bmrn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash generation is the main support. Operating cash flow was USD 576.97 million and free cash flow after plant and equipment purchases USD 498.94 million in the nine months to 2026-09-30, down 20.78% and 25.09% from a year earlier; the company attributes the lower operating cash flow mainly to lower net income and the timing of payments to vendors, partly offset by lower inventory purchases. Free cash flow excludes the USD 277.88 million paid for acquired research assets and the USD 5,067.63 million paid for Amicus, so it measures operating capacity, not total cash after deals.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_bmrn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bmrn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47; calculation C5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Growth is mostly acquired and the largest product is slowing. Revenue rose 18.49% in the nine months, but without the USD 336.42 million Amicus products contributed it rose 4.15%; VOXZOGO, 28.78% of 2025 revenues, grew 9.78% in the nine months after 26.10% in 2025. The three largest products were 68.43% of 2025 revenues, so diversification is average, not strong.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_bmrn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-K_2025-12-31_bmrn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 209; calculation C6; calculation C7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity and the 2027 maturity look manageable. Cash of USD 736.01 million alone covers the USD 660.00 million due in 2027 1.12x and cash plus the undrawn revolver covers it 2.02x; the USD 600.00 million convertible notes due in May 2027 had a fair value of 97.65% of principal, which suggests cash repayment rather than conversion. The revolver depends on covenant compliance that cannot be tested, so cash is the firmer cushion, and pro forma cash after the October 2026 licence payment is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is restrained on distributions and active in acquisitions. The company has paid no dividend and made no buyback, pre-funded the acquisition notes into escrow and cut the bridge to zero, but it bought three businesses and licensed a programme in barely more than a year and ranks secured lenders ahead of the convertible holders. Business & governance rates owner behaviour medium risk, and this analysis agrees.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case for a better view is that the covenants were met at 2026-09-30 against a 3.50x maximum, which allows 4.00x for certain acquisitions, so the contract definition of EBITDA must differ materially from reported EBITDA, although its content is not supplied; management aims for gross leverage below 2.50x by mid-2027 and expects about USD 280.00 million of GAAP cost synergies by 2028. Free cash flow of USD 498.94 million in nine months and the high gross margin support debt service, and no dividend leaves the group. That case would win if the credit agreement defines EBITDA to include the missing months of Amicus and synergies and if the fourth quarter shows interest covered comfortably.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_bmrn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 50; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_earningsrelease-6aug26ex991.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-11-02_earningsrelease-2nov26ex991.htm.jsonl, page 3; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The case against is that leverage is high on any supported measure: adding back stock-based compensation and the acquired research charge still leaves net debt at 3.88x, in the range of the stated covenant maxima of 3.50x and 4.00x, so there is little evidence of wide headroom unless the covenant definition allows further add-backs, and the 4.00x acquisition allowance is temporary. Organic revenue growth is low, VOXZOGO growth has slowed, and revenue guidance was cut. The view would worsen if fourth-quarter revenue came in at the bottom of the guided range, if a further debt-funded deal was announced, or if the credit agreement defined covenant EBITDA narrowly; it would improve on a pro forma EBITDA that shows run-rate leverage near the covenant, or on a refinancing of the 2027 notes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength: cash generation. Operating cash flow of USD 576.97 million and free cash flow of USD 498.94 million in nine months, with purchases of plant and equipment at only 3.20% of 2025 revenues, give the company internal funds for interest and scheduled amortisation, which supports deleveraging and the 2027 repayment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_bmrn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 183–184; calculation C5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength: liquidity and a pre-funded structure. Cash of USD 736.01 million, an undrawn revolver of USD 600.00 million and escrowed acquisition notes mean no funding gap before the May 2027 maturity, which lowers refinancing pressure; pro forma cash after the October 2026 licence payment is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength: a diversified rare-disease franchise with exclusivity into the 2030s. Nine commercial therapies, VOXZOGO patents to 2035 and 2036 and orphan exclusivity to 2030, and acquired Fabry and Pompe products, reduce the risk that one product loss stops debt service.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness: leverage. Net debt of USD 3,437.68 million at 9.07x trailing reported EBITDA, or USD 3,507.68 million and 9.26x pro forma for the October 2026 licence payment, with annualised coupon interest of USD 210.73 million, leaves a thin cushion against an earnings shortfall until Amicus earnings are fully counted.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness: concentration and order timing. VOXZOGO is 28.78% of revenues, three customers are 37% of net product revenues and large international orders move between quarters, so a delayed order can swing cash and covenant tests in a single quarter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-11-02_earningsrelease-2nov26ex991.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness: ranking and unseen covenants. The secured term loans rank ahead of the senior unsecured notes and the subordinated convertible notes as to collateral, and the covenants that limit further deals and distributions are not supplied, so subordinated holders carry risk they cannot measure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: BioMarin develops, makes and sells medicines for rare genetically defined diseases, with one operating segment and nine commercial therapies after the Amicus acquisition. Revenue comes from product sales to a small number of specialty pharmacies, distributors and governments, and from a collaboration in which Sanofi sells ALDURAZYME. That model gives visibility because patients are chronic and treatments are not discretionary, but it also concentrates cash flow in a few products and in lumpy government and international orders; both facts shape debt service capacity and make quarterly cover ratios unreliable.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The company is publicly held with no controlling holder identified in the sources, wholly owns Amicus, Alesta and Inozyme, and has paid no dividend. Holder percentages, board independence and related-party dealings are not supplied, and guarantor subsidiaries are unnamed, so structurally senior claims at subsidiary level cannot be sized. Financial policy is shown by behaviour: a conservative record on distributions and an acquisitive record on deals, with leverage tolerance revealed by funding about two thirds of the Amicus price with new debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Volume growth from patient additions drives VOXZOGO, while the enzyme therapies are mature; revenue is recurring, regulated and concentrated, not cyclical. The risks are price controls and special access programmes in international markets, where about 65.12% of 2025 net product revenues arose, substitution by rival products in achondroplasia, and generic competition for KUVAN. Switching costs are high for chronic enzyme therapy, which supports retention, but one international order can move revenue between quarters.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bmrn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 5–7; 10-K_2025-12-31_bmrn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19; 10-K_2025-12-31_bmrn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 209; calculation C6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Research and development and selling, general and administrative costs were 64.41% of 2025 revenues, and most are discretionary, so management can cut them if earnings fall, as it is doing after Amicus through restructuring. Cost of sales is a smaller share, giving a high gross margin, but 2026 margins carry inventory step-up amortisation, restructuring charges and integration cost. Margins can be defended under mild volume pressure through cost cuts, but acquired research purchases and fixed interest are not flexible and would dominate in a sharp revenue shortfall.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_bmrn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 181–182; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bmrn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–30; calculation C8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital spending is low at 3.20% of 2025 revenues, and free cash flow exceeded reported EBITDA in each period shown because stock-based compensation, impairments and non-cash acquired research reduce EBITDA but not operating cash. Working capital absorbs cash as receivables and inventory grow with revenue, and 2026 adds restructuring cash and higher cash interest. EBITDA translates into free cash flow that can fund debt service, but conversion will fall as annual interest reaches the annualised level.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_bmrn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation C3; calculation C5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry in achondroplasia is rising: named clinical-stage competitors are developing rival products, and a competitor's product is on the market under a royalty settlement, which caps pricing power and growth. New entrants are limited by orphan exclusivity, patents to 2035 and 2036 for VOXZOGO and the small patient pools, but exclusivity for VIMIZIM in the United States ends in 2026 and NAGLAZYME and ALDURAZYME patents have expired. Buyer power is moderate: three customers take 37% of net product revenues and governments and payers press on price. Supplier power is moderate because some raw materials come from a sole or single source and manufacture sits in two sites, which creates supply-interruption risk to cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Regulation and currency are material to credit. Government price controls and healthcare reform can cut revenue, and approvals set the pace of growth: the FDA acts on VOXZOGO applications on 2027-02-28 and 2027-05-30. About 65.12% of net product revenues arise outside the United States, mostly in euros, and cash flow hedges with a notional USD 1,748.17 million protect forecast flows for up to two years. Social and technological factors are not primary credit drivers on the provided materials.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bmrn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 5–7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bmrn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; EX-99.1_2026-11-02_earningsrelease-2nov26ex991.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths: cash conversion, low capital needs, patent and exclusivity runway for VOXZOGO, a pre-funded financing, no distributions. Weaknesses: leverage at the reported level, product and customer concentration, unseen covenants, a lower-ranked convertible. Opportunities: a new VOXZOGO indication, Amicus cost synergies of about USD 280.00 million by 2028 and pipeline readouts in 2027 and 2028, each of which would raise earnings and reduce leverage. Threats: competing achondroplasia products, price regulation, integration shortfall and further debt-funded acquisitions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale and market position is average: revenue is moderate in absolute terms, rare-disease leadership is real in several niches, and no peer comparison is supplied. Competitive advantage is average: patents and orphan exclusivity protect VOXZOGO but rivals are advancing and older enzyme patents have expired. Business diversification is average because the three largest products were 68.43% of 2025 revenues. Cost and capex flexibility is strong: capital spending is {pct(103038, 3221253)}% of revenues and research and selling costs are large and discretionary. Margin stability is average: gross margin is high but reported EBITDA margin was depressed by acquired research, restructuring and integration. Free cash flow stability is average: conversion is high, but order timing, interest and integration cash make it less predictable. Ability to refinance and access capital markets is average: the company issued senior unsecured notes in February 2026 and arranged secured loans, but leverage is high and no rating or price is supplied. Liquidity position is average: cash covers the 2027 maturity, subject to the covenant uncertainty on the revolver. Financial policy and governance is average: no distributions and escrowed financing against repeated deals and unseen covenants. The trend is deteriorating on leverage and improving on revenue, and the main missing data are pro forma EBITDA, covenant definitions and holder detail.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_bmrn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 23–25; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over 12 to 24 months the tailwinds are Amicus cost synergies, a full year of Amicus sales, the FDA action dates for VOXZOGO on 2027-02-28 and 2027-05-30, and the Ascendis royalty; the headwinds are interest on the new debt, the May 2027 convertible maturity, order timing and a lower revenue guidance range. Guidance implies fourth-quarter revenue of USD 1,019.44 million to USD 1,119.44 million against USD 1,024.65 million in the third quarter. Over three to five years the tailwinds are patent protection to 2035 and 2036 and pipeline data in 2027 and 2028; the headwinds are generic and biosimilar entry on older products, price regulation and contingent milestone obligations of up to USD 510.00 million for the Dimerix licence plus milestones on other licences.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-02_earningsrelease-2nov26ex991.htm.jsonl, pages 2–5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bmrn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-K_2025-12-31_bmrn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 23–25; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The initiating condition is a shortfall in the largest products: the delayed international VOXZOGO order slips again, or a competing achondroplasia product takes new patients, while Amicus integration costs run over. The first operational break is lower VOXZOGO and enzyme sales in a quarter, which cuts revenue and, with high fixed research and selling costs, cuts EBITDA by more than revenue. The financial transmission is lower operating cash flow against fixed interest on the new debt and scheduled amortisation, which pushes reported leverage up and puts pressure on a covenant defined on EBITDA that is not disclosed. Management levers are cuts to discretionary research and selling spend, pausing acquired research purchases, and drawing the revolver, but the revolver is only available while covenants are met. The resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress through 2027, because cash alone covers the principal due, but the refinancing of the May 2027 notes and any covenant breach are the observable triggers.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-11-02_earningsrelease-2nov26ex991.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bmrn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 50; calculation C2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, BioMarin presents an adequate business profile supported by cash generation, low capital needs, a diversified rare-disease portfolio with long patent protection and a pre-funded financing, but credit quality is constrained by high leverage after the Amicus acquisition, concentration in VOXZOGO and a few customers, and covenants that are not visible. Cash-flow durability appears adequate due to high conversion of EBITDA to free cash flow, with order timing and rising interest as the swing factors. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on delivery of Amicus earnings, covenant headroom and market access ahead of the May 2027 convertible maturity. The primary downside path is a revenue shortfall in VOXZOGO or the enzyme therapies against the new fixed interest burden, which would push reported leverage up and test an undisclosed covenant. Further analysis would require pro forma EBITDA, the credit agreement and its definitions, and the proxy statement. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: leverage after the Amicus financing on an earnings base that is not yet pro forma.
